pharm: Selective intestinal cholesterol absorption inhibitor (NPC1L1 antagonist)
quick: 10 mg once daily (alone or added to a statin)
May take with or without food
Insufficient data; avoid combination with statins in pregnancy
Unknown if excreted in human milk; weigh benefit/risk
Not recommended in moderate-to-severe hepatic impairment
No specific interaction; moderate intake re: lipids
Lipid panel; liver enzymes when used with a statin or fenofibrate; CK if muscle symptoms
summary: Ezetimibe is a once-daily cholesterol absorption inhibitor that lowers LDL-C by blocking intestinal cholesterol uptake via the NPC1L1 transporter. It is used as an adjunct to diet, in combination with a statin (or alone when statins are not tolerable), and in homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia/sitosterolemia. It is generally well tolerated; most serious risks (hepatic and muscle effects) relate to combination with a statin or fenofibrate.
indications: Adjunct to diet to reduce elevated LDL-C in primary hyperlipidemia (including heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia), with a statin or alone
With a statin in pediatric patients >=10 years with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia
With atorvastatin or simvastatin for homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HoFH)
With fenofibrate as an adjunct to diet for mixed hyperlipidemia

dosage.t: With or without food, at any time of day
dosage.n: May be given with a statin or fenofibrate; can be co-administered with bile acid sequestrants if dosed >=2 h before or >=4 h after
As part of combination LDL-lowering regimen

admin: Take 10 mg once daily, with or without food
If used with a bile acid sequestrant, take ezetimibe at least 2 hours before or at least 4 hours after the sequestrant
When combined, follow the prescribing information and dose limits of the statin or fenofibrate
moa: Ezetimibe reduces blood cholesterol by inhibiting the intestinal absorption of cholesterol. Its molecular target is the sterol transporter Niemann-Pick C1-Like 1 (NPC1L1), which mediates intestinal uptake of cholesterol and phytosterols. This decreases delivery of cholesterol to the liver, increases hepatic LDL receptor expression, and lowers plasma LDL-C; it is complementary to statins (which reduce synthesis).

absolute: When combined with a statin/fenofibrate: any contraindication to that co-administered agent (e.g., active liver disease/unexplained persistent transaminase elevations with a statin; pregnancy/lactation with a statin)
monitor: Liver enzymes when combined with a statin or fenofibrate

preg: There are insufficient data on ezetimibe alone in pregnancy. When co-administered with a statin it is contraindicated in pregnancy (statins). Use ezetimibe in pregnancy only if clearly needed and not with a statin.
lact: It is not known whether ezetimibe is excreted in human milk. When used with a statin, breastfeeding is not recommended. Weigh benefits against potential risk.
renal: No dosage adjustment is required in renal impairment. When combined with a statin, observe the statin's renal-related dosing cautions.
hepatic: No adjustment in mild hepatic impairment, but ezetimibe is NOT recommended in patients with moderate or severe hepatic impairment because of unknown effects of increased exposure.

major: Cyclosporine - increases ezetimibe (and cyclosporine) exposure; monitor cyclosporine levels
Combination with a statin or fenofibrate - increases risk of myopathy/rhabdomyolysis and hepatic enzyme abnormalities (follow that drug's PI)
moderate: Fenofibrate (may increase cholesterol excretion into bile - cholelithiasis risk)
minor: Bile acid sequestrants (cholestyramine) reduce ezetimibe absorption - separate dosing
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food (food does not meaningfully affect exposure)
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction; moderate intake advisable for lipid control
interactions.diagnostics: Lipid panel; liver function tests when used with statin/fenofibrate; CK if muscle symptoms

serious: Hepatic enzyme elevations (especially with a statin)

monitoring: Fasting lipid panel (baseline and to assess response)
Liver function tests when used in combination with a statin or fenofibrate
Creatine kinase (CK) if unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness occurs
counsel: Take once daily at the same time, with or without food
Continue your cholesterol-lowering diet and other lifestyle measures
Report unexplained muscle pain/weakness, dark urine, yellowing of the skin/eyes, or severe stomach pain
If you also take a bile acid resin (cholestyramine), separate the doses by at least 2-4 hours
Tell your doctor about all medicines, especially statins, fibrates, and cyclosporine
pearls: Ezetimibe complements statins: it blocks intestinal cholesterol absorption while statins reduce synthesis, giving additive LDL-C lowering (~15-20% added LDL reduction on top of a statin; IMPROVE-IT showed CV benefit added to simvastatin).
Most serious adverse effects (transaminase rise, myopathy/rhabdomyolysis) arise from the co-administered statin or fibrate - monitor accordingly.
Separate from bile acid sequestrants (take ezetimibe >=2 h before or >=4 h after) to avoid reduced absorption.
Not recommended in moderate-severe hepatic impairment.
missed: Take the missed dose when remembered the same day; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip it and resume the regular schedule. Do not double up.
overdose: Limited data; ezetimibe was generally well tolerated at higher doses in studies. In case of overdose, provide symptomatic and supportive care and monitor as needed.
